findings.claim: The stick's launcher (deploy/launcher.sh, copied as install) is code from the stick, so any check it makes protects only an honest launcher; ruled by the integrator: accepted for a supervised PoC on synthetic data, the anchor outside the stick is the delivery sheet (the launcher's sha256, first 24 hex, beside the key's fingerprint, and a line with stock tools that runs a private copy only after the code is confirmed), and the launcher pins the vendor key's fingerprint
deploy/bootstrap.sh ended with exec, so its EXIT trap never ran and every run left its temp folder, with the unpacked host tree, behind; fixed in HS-1
A bare machine with no Docker still stops in deploy/box-install.sh with a message that names box-prepare.sh with --pub; design row 53's second half is not removed by HS-1
RUNBOOK section 1 (docs/runbook/01-install-a-new-site.md) still writes only the long first command; the one command is not on the runbook page
The fingerprint's form; ruled by the integrator: the first 24 hex digits (96 bits) of the sha256 of the key's DER form, in six groups of four, the same on the sheet and the screen

bash read deploy/launcher.sh from the stick as it ran, so a line written into the stick's install during the fingerprint question ran after the signature check; fixed: the body is a function called on the last line

No test held the launcher's copy-then-verify-then-run order: 8 of 8 of the independent review's mutants survived; fixed: a swap of the stick's bootstrap, .sig and key during the question, and a check that openssl reads only the private copies
The launcher copied the stick's bootstrap, .sig and key whole, following links, before any check; fixed: a link or a file over 256 KiB stops with nothing changed
A stick path with a space was refused by tools/apply_update.sh only after /opt/trialbox was unpacked and the key placed; fixed: the launcher and the bootstrap refuse it before anything is written
